quickAnswerTitle: How Utah School Calendars Work in 2026–27
quickAnswer: Utah does not use one statewide first day, spring break, or last day. Each local education agency approves its calendar in an open meeting, while Utah's pupil-accounting rule generally requires at least 180 school days and adequate contingency days. District calendars can still differ in opening dates, breaks, professional-development days, parent-teacher conference schedules, A/B rotations, shortened days, and weather make-up plans. MySchoolDates currently has reviewed district resources for Alpine, Davis, Granite, Jordan, Canyons, and Weber.
about:
Utah public school calendars are adopted locally rather than through one uniform statewide schedule. The Utah State Board of Education publishes district and charter calendar resources, but families still need the calendar adopted by their school district or charter school for actual attendance dates.

State pupil-accounting rules provide the common framework. An LEA generally provides educational services over at least 180 school days, approves instructional time and its school calendar in an open meeting, and includes adequate contingency days to reduce the need for a waiver after closures. The rules also distinguish ordinary attendance days from professional-development, parent-teacher conference, emergency, and distance-learning arrangements.

Those statewide rules do not make district calendars interchangeable. Alpine publishes A/B labels and a separate K/PreK assessment opening; Davis layers secondary A/B days, Wednesday late starts, and Friday elementary early dismissal; Granite separates grade-band conferences; Jordan staggers openings by level; Canyons excludes Brighton High School from its K-12 quarter calendar in favor of a separate trimester calendar; and Weber combines a daily A/B grid with Wednesday early outs at different elementary and secondary times. Families should start with the district page, then check the assigned school for bell times, testing, activities, and campus-specific changes.
calendarRulesDescription: Utah combines statewide pupil-accounting requirements with calendars approved by local education agencies. These distinctions help explain why nearby districts can publish different schedules.

calendarRules.label: Calendars are approved locally
calendarRules.description: An LEA governing board approves total instructional time and the school calendar in an open meeting, so Utah does not have one statewide set of attendance dates.

calendarRules.label: General 180-day minimum
calendarRules.description: Utah's pupil-accounting rule generally requires an LEA to provide educational services over at least 180 school days, subject to the exceptions allowed by law and rule.

calendarRules.label: Contingency days matter
calendarRules.description: LEA boards are expected to provide adequate contingency school days. A date labeled as a possible make-up day remains conditional until the district announces that it will be used.

calendarRules.label: Staff and conference days need context
calendarRules.description: Professional-development, teacher-preparation, parent-teacher conference, and staff workdays may use different attendance labels. Families should not infer student attendance from a generic calendar title alone.

stateSections.label: How Utah Approves and Counts School Calendars
stateSections.content:
Utah Administrative Rule R277-419 requires an LEA to approve its total instructional time and school calendar in an open meeting. The same rule generally requires at least 180 school days and directs governing boards to include adequate contingency days. This creates a common accountability framework without imposing identical first days, breaks, staff days, or last days statewide.

USBE also publishes separate yearly district and charter calendar resources. Those statewide summaries are useful for finding an LEA, but the district or charter's current calendar remains the better source for grade-specific openings, shortened days, A/B rotations, and revisions.

stateSections.label: Alpine School District Changes After 2026–27
stateSections.content: Alpine School District's 2026–27 calendar is its final operating-year calendar. The district says it will operate schools through June 30, 2027, and Aspen Peaks, Lake Mountain, and Timpanogos school districts begin operations July 1. Families in the current Alpine area will need the calendar published by the successor district assigned to their school for 2027–28. A future-year recommendations document is not treated as an adopted student calendar.

faqs.q: Are Utah school calendars the same statewide?
faqs.a: No. Utah LEA governing boards approve their own calendars in open meetings. First days, breaks, staff days, parent-teacher conference schedules, possible make-up days, and last days can differ by district or charter school.
Utah Administrative Rule R277-419 generally requires an LEA to provide educational services over at least 180 school days, subject to the exceptions allowed by law and rule.

faqs.q: When do Utah public schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: There is no single statewide first day. Each district or charter school adopts its own calendar. Alpine School District starts most students August 19, 2026, while its K and PreK students use an assessment window before beginning regular attendance August 25.

faqs.q: When is Utah Spring Break in 2027?
faqs.a: Utah does not have one statewide Spring Break. Families should select their district or charter calendar because break dates and adjacent staff days can differ.

faqs.q: Can weather change a Utah school calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Utah rules direct LEAs to include adequate contingency school days, but a possible make-up date remains conditional until the district announces that it will be used.

faqs.q: Where can families find official Utah school calendars?
faqs.a: The Utah State Board of Education publishes district and charter calendar resources. For detailed attendance dates and later revisions, use the official calendar page for the student's district, charter, school, or program.

faqs.q: Can I add a Utah school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Reviewed MySchoolDates district pages provide an ICS file that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. It is a one-time import, not a live district subscription.
